items.evidence_quote: Observed facts: two distinct spermatic-cord structures were identified, each containing a vas and vascular/neural elements, both traced toward the testis through a common internal ring.
items.reason: All statements are accurate to the vignette; observed facts, hypotheses, and general knowledge are explicitly separated.

items.evidence_quote: Hypotheses: the finding is most consistent with either a duplicated spermatic cord supplying a single testis or polyorchidism with two testes sharing a common internal ring. These cannot be distinguished from the description alone.
items.reason: Inferences are clinically defensible and explicitly tied to the limited evidence, with competing interpretations acknowledged without overstating conclusions.

items.evidence_quote: Immediate safety priorities: neither cord should be ligated, divided, or mobilised beyond what is necessary for hernia repair until the relationship to the testis or testes is confirmed.
items.reason: Premises are established before conclusions; safety priorities follow logically from the anatomical uncertainty.

items.evidence_quote: Further confirmation: direct inspection of the testis or testes at the time of surgery is the most immediate step.
items.reason: Every section serves a distinct clinical purpose with no redundancy.
